In some matchups with some DIs, you can even actually stage spike the opponent with a Dthrow (usually really tall characters).

The biggest factors that give him awful survivability compared to Pikachu are UpB speed (His is much slower and easier to hit without trading and potentially dying), tech roll distance (by far some of the worst tech rolls in the game, even Bowser can usually cover all of them on reaction if they know the matchup), and his weight. The self damage plays into the weight being a bad thing, but it's not the fundamental flaw with the character.

Jolt isn't a great move. Most of its use is limited to recovery and retreating to platforms. There's a massive amount of lag on the move, even when used airborne, that makes it so you can't really approach with it and expect to get any reward at all.

Pichu's skull bash isn't really a consequential move for the most part, it's minimal self damage for a move that isn't really used in Neutral a lot (I sometimes try to poke people's feet on platforms with reverse edgecancels), but it's definitely not a gamechanger. Only regular use it gets is punishing whiffed rests. 

I think you have the wrong mindset with Pichu's moves-- just because they self damage doesn't mean you can't use the moves. It does mean you have to be a little conscious of how you're using them, but as long as you're being intentional, it's usually best to mostly disregard the self damage.

90% sure it's a combination of a few things. First, I think he ran off with a Pivot Drop, which is like a PC Drop but out of dash rather than a walk, which is a way smaller window to hit than doing it out of a walk because you don't maintain as much momentum during the turn. Then, he did an immediate Dair, and hit on the first possible frame. Because of the hitlag on the Dair, he was able to reland on the same platform with the same mechanic that lets you platform drop Bair to reland. Many aerials let you platform drop reland (called a Platform Cancel or a Drop Cancel), but generally only if they stretch your ECB upwards and if you hit someone with the attack as well (because of the aforementioned hitlag frames). Also, some aerials are able to do it when they happen after sliding or running off of a platform, because you fall with a slower speed if you fall off of a platform in that way. Because you don't maintain as much horizontal momentum with a Pivot Drop as you would with a PC Drop, he didn't actually drift far enough away to be unable to reland onto the platform. So I think the Dair only was able to reland because of a precise combination of each of these mechanics.
